rationale: The Agreement grants SFJ no audit, inspection or verification right against PB. Article 9 (Records) imposes only mutual record-keeping and retention obligations (Sections 9.1 and 9.2) with no accompanying right of access, examination or on-site review. Section 3.6 ("Audits") does not create any SFJ audit right over PB either: each Party audits its own Permitted Third Parties (3.6.1) and PB audits its own manufacturing facilities (3.6.2), in each case simply sharing the resulting audit reports; similarly, Section 3.5.5 only requires exchange of source data verification reports. The affirmative covenants in Section 7.6, unusually for a secured financing, contain no lender-style inspection/books-and-records access right, and the financial information flow in Section 3.18.2 is limited to delivery of PB's own financial statements plus periodic executive meetings — reporting, not auditing. There is therefore no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or systems-access exposure to constrain, and nothing in the walk-away zone (no unlimited, unannounced or remote-access audit rights). This position is better for us than the playbook's preferred outcome, so no redline is warranted; we would resist any SFJ attempt to add an audit or inspection right, and if one is introduced we would require it to be limited to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at SFJ's cost absent a >5% discrepancy, with no direct access to PB systems.

Section 3.18.2 is financial reporting plus executive meetings, not an audit right. No frequency, notice, cost-allocation or systems-access exposure exists, and nothing falls in the walk-away zone; the absence of any audit right binding our party is better than the playbook's preferred position, so no redline is warranted (and flagging would be over-flagging a clause that benefits us). quote: 15.9 Governing Law. quote: 13.5 SFJ Representation, Warranty and Covenant. SFJ hereby represents, warrants and covenants that it will have, as and when needed, sufficient funds to satisfy its obligations hereunder.
rationale: SFJ performs real work for PB — the "SFJ Services" (global CRO oversight and execution of the Clinical Trials in the European Clinical Trial Countries, Japan and China) plus primary responsibility for the Phase 3 Trial in the Designated Asian Countries — yet the only SFJ-specific warranty in Article 13 is the funding warranty in 13.5. The nearest performance standards are covenants only: 3.1.4 (material compliance with Applicable Laws) and 3.1.5 (Commercially Reasonable Efforts to conduct the Clinical Trials in accordance with the SFJ SOPs). There is no express warranty of workmanlike performance or conformance, and no warranty remedy, so the clause fails even the fallback (which still requires a conformance warranty with repair/re-perform/refund). The exposure is compounded by 13.6.2, whose all-caps disclaimer carves out only what is "SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 13", leaving nothing in Article 13 to stand behind SFJ's performance. We therefore inserted the warranty into Section 13.5 itself so it automatically falls inside the 13.6.2 carve-out (no separate change to the disclaimer needed), tailored to the services actually rendered (SFJ SOPs, Protocol, Applicable Law including GCP/ICH) with re-performance at SFJ's cost, and excluded from Development Costs so PB does not fund the fix. No fixed months-long warranty period is proposed because the obligations are continuous trial-conduct obligations rather than a delivered deliverable.
